proofs.full_local_argument: Write G_t=sum_{s=1}^t X_s X_s^T, Z_t=sum_{s=1}^t eta_s X_s and H_t=lambda I_d+G_t=V_t. First suppose R>0. For deterministic q in R^d define L_t(q)=exp(q^T Z_t/R - q^T G_t q/2), with L_0(q)=1. Conditional on F_{t-1}, a_t=q^T X_t is measurable. The conditional MGF assumption implies E[exp(a_t eta_t/R-a_t^2/2)|F_{t-1}]<=1. Its validity for an arbitrary finite predictable a_t follows first for countably valued simple approximations and then by conditional Fatou as a_t^{(n)} tends to a_t; the MGF bound exp((a_t^{(n)})^2/2) tends to exp(a_t^2/2). Thus L_t(q) is a nonnegative supermartingale and E L_t(q)<=1. All X_t take finite values in R^d; no deterministic bound on their norms or invertibility of G_t is needed. Let pi be the fixed N(0,(lambda I_d)^{-1}) probability law and set M_t=int L_t(q) pi(dq). Conditional Tonelli and the preceding inequality show that M_t is a nonnegative supermartingale with M_0=1. In particular it is integrable. Complete the square directly in the exponent q^T Z_t/R-q^T H_t q/2: it equals -(q-H_t^{-1}Z_t/R)^T H_t(q-H_t^{-1}Z_t/R)/2 + Z_t^T H_t^{-1}Z_t/(2R^2). Since H_t is positive definite, Gaussian integration gives M_t=sqrt(det(lambda I_d)/det(H_t))*exp(||Z_t||_{H_t^{-1}}^2/(2R^2)). This identity uses no inverse of G_t, including at t=0. Fix delta in (0,1) and define tau as the first integer t>=0 for which ||Z_t||_{H_t^{-1}}^2>2R^2 log(det(H_t)^(1/2)/(lambda^(d/2)delta)); set tau=infinity if no crossing occurs. This is a stopping time since each finite-time inequality is F_t-measurable. On {tau<=n}, M_{tau}>1/delta. For each finite n the stopped process M_{t min tau} has conditional mean at most its preceding value: multiply the supermartingale increment by the F_{t-1}-measurable indicator {tau>=t}. Iterating yields E M_{tau min n}<=1. Consequently P(tau<=n)<=delta E[M_{tau min n} 1_{tau<=n}]<=delta. Increasing n to infinity gives P(tau<infinity)<=delta, without evaluating any matrix or exponential at infinite time. Hence, on one event of probability at least 1-delta, for all finite t, ||Z_t||_{H_t^{-1}}<=R sqrt(2 log(det(H_t)^(1/2)/(lambda^(d/2)delta))). The log is positive because det(H_t)>=lambda^d and delta<1. If R=0, the MGF bound gives for every t, epsilon>0 and u>0, P(eta_t>=epsilon)<=exp(-u epsilon), and the same bound holds for -eta_t. Let u tend to infinity and use countably many positive rational epsilon and integer t; then eta_t=0 for all t almost surely. Thus Z_t=0 for every t and the same noise bound holds with right side zero. Finally the observation identity gives b_t=G_t theta_*+Z_t, so theta_hat_t-theta_*=H_t^{-1}(Z_t-lambda theta_*). By the triangle inequality, ||theta_hat_t-theta_*||_{H_t}<=||Z_t||_{H_t^{-1}}+lambda||theta_*||_{H_t^{-1}}. Since H_t>=lambda I_d, H_t^{-1}<=lambda^{-1} I_d, and the second term is at most sqrt(lambda)||theta_*||_2<=sqrt(lambda)S. On the same event this proves the exact stated determinant radius for every integer t>=0, including the empty-sum case. All parameters are fixed as in the statement. This proves only the determinant assertion; no conclusion about the separately transcribed additional radius is made.

assumptions: Fixed unknown theta_* in R^d with ||theta_*||_2<=S. Let (F_t)_{t>=0} be a filtration; X_t is F_{t-1}-measurable and eta_t is F_t-measurable. For every t>=1 and real u, E[exp(u eta_t)|F_{t-1}]<=exp(u^2R^2/2) almost surely. Observe Y_t=<X_t,theta_*>+eta_t.
lambda>0 is fixed before observations. No uniform action-norm bound is required for the determinant-form assertion.
Only for the additional printed assertion: finite L>=0 satisfies ||X_t||_2<=L almost surely for every t>=1.
statement.conclusion: First source assertion: P(for every t>=0, ||theta_hat_t-theta_*||_{V_t}<=r_t)>=1-delta. Additional printed assertion, recorded without endorsement: under the L assumption, with probability >=1-delta for every t>=0 the same error is <=R sqrt(d log((1+tL^2/lambda)/delta))+sqrt(lambda)S. This additional radius is not asserted here as a valid consequence or looser version of the determinant radius; its normalization remains unresolved.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For positive definite A, ||z||_A=sqrt(z^T A z). V_t=lambda I_d+sum_{s=1}^t X_s X_s^T; b_t=sum_{s=1}^t X_sY_s; theta_hat_t=V_t^{-1}b_t. Empty sums are zero. Define r_t=R sqrt(2 log(det(V_t)^(1/2)/(lambda^(d/2)delta)))+sqrt(lambda)S and C_t={theta in R^d: ||theta_hat_t-theta||_{V_t}<=r_t}.
statement.parameter_domains: Integer d>=1; lambda>0; finite R>=0,S>=0; delta in (0,1); optional finite L>=0; integer t>=0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed choice of parameters and process satisfying the assumptions, and every fixed delta in (0,1), the source asserts probability at least 1-delta simultaneously for all integer t>=0, separately for each displayed assertion. No uniformity over data-chosen lambda or delta is inferred. The source prints delta>0; this record uses the meaningful confidence range (0,1).

supplemental_proof_map.limits: The printed Appendix A scales by R and uses an intermediate inverse of unregularized G_t, which can be singular; it also writes stopping-time expressions at infinity. The local proof below avoids these issues by using only lambda I+G_t and bounded stopping times, and handles R=0 separately. No full-rank, bounded-design or positive-noise assumption is added. Appendix C and later proofs were not extracted.
supplemental_proof_map.locator: Official supplemental PDF Appendix A pp.11–13; Appendix B p.13 and ending p.14.
map: Appendix A p.11 Lemma 8: conditional MGF gives a nonnegative exponential supermartingale; stopping and Fatou bound its expectation.

Appendix A pp.11–12 Lemma 9: mix over an independent centered Gaussian with covariance V^{-1}; Gaussian integration yields sqrt(det(V)/det(V+G_t))*exp(||S_t||^2_{(V+G_t)^{-1}}/(2R^2)); Markov gives a stopping-time tail bound.
Appendix A pp.12–13: first threshold-crossing stopping time converts that bound to the time-uniform Theorem 1 statement.
Appendix B p.13: Lemma 10 bounds determinant by trace using arithmetic-geometric means. Theorem 2 expands ridge error, bounds the regularization bias by sqrt(lambda)S and applies Theorem 1.

Appendix B p.14 ending: set x=V_t(theta_hat_t-theta_*), then divide by the error norm to obtain the determinant ellipsoid. Zero error is immediate. The next sentence asserts a similar second bound but does not derive its constants.
